title.narrative: Polychlorinated Biphenyls-free Indonesia: Financing a shift to more efficient energy systems through the elimination of related waste and contaminated equipment

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The design of the PCB project in Indonesia has considered socio-economic benefits as a key aspect of its execution strategy. By integrating gender considerations into its design and implementation, the PCB project also aims not only to achieve environmental and economic goals but also to promote benefits to relevant women’s participation. These benefits have been thoroughly analyzed and detailed in the Project Description. Specific aspects include:Capacity Building:• Training programs for national stakeholders, including government agencies, PCB owners and waste management professionals will enhance knowledge and technical capacity in safely handling and disposing of PCBs.• Increased national expertise in PCB decontamination can contribute to sustainable practices beyond the project's timeline.• Public awareness on the risks and safe management of PCBs will empower communities to advocate for environmental and health rights.Gender-Responsive Approach:• The project will apply a gender lens to all activities, ensuring that the design and implementation address the specific needs and contributions of men and women.• Gender-sensitive indicators will be included in monitoring frameworks to track participation, benefits, and impacts on women and men.Monitoring and ReportingThe socio-economic and gender-inclusive impacts of the project will be monitored at key stages:• Mid-Term Review (MTR): Progress on gender equity and socio-economic benefits will be assessed, and strategies will be refined if needed. • Terminal Evaluation (TE): A final evaluation will measure the overall impact, with lessons documented to inform future gender-responsive GEF projects.
To establish a sustainable system for the fulfilment of the Stockholm Convention deadline on PCB in Indonesia, with the direct ESM disposal of not less than 10,000 tons of PCB
